answers.answer:
All three domains share SCOPe family a.298.1.1 (TAL (transcription activator-like) effector) in release 2.08, the current release per the API. Family is SCOPe's strongest evolutionary level: it means a clear common ancestry, not just similar shape. Superfamily a.298.1 (parent node 267596) and fold a.298 (class a, all-alpha) are weaker levels that the family sits under. Sequence length is not a membership criterion here. The shared unit is the tandem repeat module of TAL effectors, a helix-turn-helix repeat of roughly 34 residues that stacks into a superhelix. Natural TAL-like proteins carry variable numbers of these repeats, so the length of a classified domain mostly tracks how many repeats its region spans.

The API's SEQRES sequences show this. d2kq5a_ (PthA, Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri; 51 residues) contains about one and a half repeats, since it has one full ~34-residue repeat followed by a truncated copy. d3v6pa_ (dHax3, Xanthomonas; 373 residues) contains about eleven repeats. d4cj9a_ (BurrH, Burkholderia rhizoxinica TaxId 412963; 752 residues) contains about twenty-two repeats. The repeat-level sequence pattern (for example the conserved 'LTP..VVAIAS..GG.KQALETV..LP..C..GLT' motif) recurs in all three, which is why they fall in one family despite the length spread. Repeat count is not a family criterion, and each domain entry covers whatever repeat region was classified.

Limits: (1) Family membership supports shared architecture and probable common origin for the repeat module, not identical function or DNA target. Target specificity in TAL effectors is set by the hypervariable repeat-variable diresidue (RVD) at repeat positions 12-13, and different RVDs (e.g., NI, NG, HD, NN) bind different bases. Do not transfer a DNA-binding target from one member to another based on the family assignment alone. (2) Length and boundary differences are not evidence of a different family; the 51-residue d2kq5a_ fragment is not a representative of full-length arrays, so use the longer arrays when reasoning about overall architecture. (3) The lengths returned are SEQRES-derived sequence lengths. They do not confirm how many residues have resolved coordinates, and I did not check coverage. (4) Shared family does not require the same host or genus; the Burkholderia member is classified with the Xanthomonas members, which supports repeat-based homology across bacterial genera. (5) Confirming any specific DNA-binding or transcriptional-activation role requires external experimental evidence, such as DNA-binding assays with defined RVD/target pairs, reporter-based activation assays, or structures of repeat-DNA complexes. Classification alone does not provide that evidence.

(2) Length and boundary differences are not evidence of a different family; the 51-residue d2kq5a_ fragment is not a representative of full-length arrays, so use the longer arrays when reasoning about overall architecture. (3) The lengths returned are SEQRES-derived sequence lengths. They do not confirm how many residues have resolved coordinates, and I did not check coverage. (4) Shared family does not require the same host or genus; the Burkholderia member is classified with the Xanthomonas members, which supports repeat-based homology across bacterial genera. (5) Confirming any specific DNA-binding or transcriptional-activation role requires external experimental evidence, such as DNA-binding assays with defined RVD/target pairs, reporter-based activation assays, or structures of repeat-DNA complexes. Classification alone does not provide that evidence.
